records.name: Greater Bustleton Civic League
records.summary: If you care about what gets built near you, Greater Bustleton Civic League is a City registered community organization in the Upper Far Northeast part of the city that hears about zoning and development proposals.
records.what_you_do: Members are volunteer Bustleton residents who talk over public safety, zoning, crime, cleanliness and development at monthly meetings, in person or by Zoom.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the fourth Tuesday at 7 pm, in person in the credit union community room or by Zoom.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Community Room, American Heritage Credit Union, 2060 Red Lion Road, Philadelphia, PA 19115

first_step.how: Come to the fourth Tuesday meeting at 7 pm in the credit union community room at 2060 Red Lion Road, or join by Zoom. The site has a membership form you can read first.
first_step.basis: The meeting time, place and a Zoom option are published openly, and a membership form is online, but the site does not say whether non-members may attend.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings start at 7 pm on the fourth Tuesday, in person or by Zoom. The group is run by volunteer Bustleton residents, and its agendas are posted on the site. The site does not say how long meetings run or whether there are dues.
first_visit_tips: Email gbustletoncl@gmail.com or use the contact form to ask whether guests are welcome before your first meeting
Check the Meeting Info page for the Zoom details if you cannot come in person

records.name: Somerton Civic Association
records.summary: A neighborhood group the City of Philadelphia has registered to be consulted on zoning and development in the Upper Far Northeast part of the city, Somerton Civic Association gives neighbors a place to hear about projects and respond.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer members talk over neighborhood events and issues at monthly meetings, often with invited speakers and elected officials, and bring local problems to them and to the police.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the second Tuesday at 7 pm at the Walker Lodge, plus special meetings as needed.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Walker Lodge of the I.O.O.F., 1290 Southampton Road, Phila., PA 19116

cost.text: Annual dues of $5 per household, covering up to two members, running September through August.

first_step.how: Attend the second Tuesday meeting at 7 pm at the Walker Lodge, 1290 Southampton Road. The site invites Somerton residents to come to a monthly meeting to join.
first_step.basis: The site invites residents to attend a monthly meeting in order to join, says new members can vote at the meeting after they join, and gives an email contact.
first_step.what_to_expect: The meeting starts at 7 pm at the Walker Lodge and is often joined by invited speakers, elected officials or their staff, and a local police meeting. The board meets before each member meeting. Dues are $5 a year per household if you decide to join.
first_visit_tips: Bring $5 in case you decide to join, since dues run September through August
Email civicsomerton@gmail.com with questions before the meeting, since the site asks for email rather than calls

records.name: Awbury Arboretum Neighbors
records.summary: Awbury Arboretum Neighbors is a neighbors group for East Germantown, founded in 1974, that sends out newsletters and meeting notices and meets online each month to talk over local issues, including zoning and development.
records.what_you_do: Members and neighbors hear from speakers at a monthly Zoom meeting, read the newsletter and meeting notices, and talk over zoning, development and neighborhood news.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the second Wednesday at 7 pm, held on Zoom.

cost.text: Annual dues: $20 family, $25 contributing, $10 for members 65 and older, $50 business.

first_step.how: Join the Zoom meeting on the second Wednesday at 7 pm; the link is on the home page. To become a member, pay annual dues by PayPal or by check to the P.O. Box, and send your name, phone, email and mailing address.
first_step.basis: The home page publishes the Zoom link for the monthly meeting and the site lists membership steps, but it does not say whether non-members may attend or who may join.
first_step.what_to_expect: The monthly meeting is held on Zoom at 7 pm on the second Wednesday, and the October 14, 2026 meeting will cover City registered community organization issues. Recent speakers have included city council members, a state representative, a city department head, and the arboretum director. Dues are paid once a year, from $10 for members 65 and older to $50 for a business.
first_visit_tips: Open the Zoom link a few minutes early to check your connection
Email aaneighbors@mail.com if you are not sure whether guests are welcome

records.name: Chew and Belfield Neighbors Club Incorporated
records.summary: Chew and Belfield Neighbors Club is a nonprofit founded in 1981 that runs neighborhood cleanups, free tutoring and classes, and job help, and holds a free summer clothing and furniture giveaway.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors volunteer on cleanups, tree plantings and block work, and can get free tutoring, GED help, and job or resume help. The club meets monthly, and membership is $12 a year for the whole household.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the last Wednesday at 6 pm; neighborhood cleanups about every other Wednesday; free tutoring and classes run October through April.

locations.label: Contact address (City list)
locations.address: 6211 Chew Ave, PO Box 14134, Philadelphia PA 19138

cost.text: Membership is $12 a year for the whole household; the club's services are free.

first_step.how: Contact the club by phone or its contact form to ask about the next cleanup, meeting, or tutoring session. Students sign up for tutoring. To join, contact the club, since the site describes no separate sign-up.
first_step.basis: Services are free and the site invites people to get in touch about upcoming events, but it does not say whether monthly meetings are open to non-members.
first_step.what_to_expect: Monthly meetings are at 6 pm on the last Wednesday in the Wissahickon Charter School gymnasium. Cleanups happen about every other Wednesday, and tutoring runs October through April for students aged 7 to 99. Membership is $12 a year for the household, and the services are free.
first_visit_tips: Call the club to confirm the date of the next meeting or cleanup before you come
Ask about access when you call, since the site does not describe it
Have $12 ready if you decide to join as a member

records.name: Community Schools @George Washington High School
records.summary: George Washington High School is one of the City's Community Schools, where volunteers help with after school and family programs. Open shifts are listed on the City's volunteer portal.
records.what_you_do: Help with school based programs for students and families.

first_step.how: Ask about open volunteer roles by email to the school's listed contact, or through the City's Community Schools program office at commschools@phila.gov or (215) 683-6012.
first_step.basis: The volunteer listing asks for several district and state clearances before a shift, so the way in needs approval first. The City program page names its office for volunteer questions but describes no open visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: The volunteer listing asks for the district's code of conduct and a volunteer certificate, a fingerprint or FBI check, a child abuse history clearance, a state criminal background check, and a City release waiver. Ask the school's coordinator which of these your role needs before you sign up for a shift.
first_visit_tips: Start the clearance paperwork early, since the listing names several
Email with questions first so you know which program needs help
